column3: Close to the Hebrew; “all the harm which I am planning to do” is rendered “all the adversities which I purpose to bring.”
Close to the Hebrew; “from the mouth of Jeremiah” is rendered “at the instruction of Jeremiah.”
Close to the Hebrew; “shut up” is rendered “confined.”
Close to the Hebrew; “from my mouth” is rendered “at my instruction,” and “a day of fasting” “the day of fasting.”
The Hebrew “perhaps their supplication will fall before Yahweh” is rendered “they will present their supplication before the LORD.”
In the Hebrew “all the people” are the subject who proclaimed the fast; NKJV makes them the recipients: “proclaimed a fast … to all the people.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the officials” is rendered “the princes.”
Close to the Hebrew; “they were in dread each to his neighbor” is rendered “they looked in fear from one to another.”
Close to the Hebrew; “from his mouth” is rendered “at his instruction.”
Close to the Hebrew; “on the scroll” is rendered “in the book.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the fire-pot was kindled before him” is rendered “a fire burning on the hearth before him.”
NKJV renders “three doors and four” as “three or four columns” and supplies “the king” as the one who cut the scroll.
Close to the Hebrew; “return, take” is rendered “Take yet another scroll.”
Close to the Hebrew; “from it” (the land) is rendered “from here.”
